plain: Failing before it can succeed or come to anything.

webster.text: Brought forth in an immature state; failing, or coming to naught, before it is complete.

more.text: Failing in its effect; miscarrying; producing nothing; as an abortive scheme.
Rendering abortive; as abortive gulf, in Milton, but not legitimate.
In botany, an abortive flower is one which falls without producing fruit.
That which is brought forth or born prematurely.

example.quote: If this do take place, if all the states combine, if all oppose, the whole will not eat up the members, but the measure which is opposed to the sense of the people will prove abortive.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Connecticut Convention, OLIVER ELSWORTH, January 1788 (Elliot prints only the opening date, January 4, 1788) (2d ed. 1836)
